A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text and Appendices A-I. Figures, tables, equations and experiments can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: Sections 4-5 and the appendices report original experiments on in-context regression, OpenWebText language modeling and time-series forecasting, including performance curves and timing measurements.

after.justification: The same original experimental results remain in Sections 4-5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The scoring functions, BTT/MLR constructions and training procedures are unchanged. Calling MLR 'contiguous' clarifies the unpermuted structure already specified in v1; it does not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic in-context linear regression, OpenWebText, the Chronos synthetic/real data mixture and ETTh1. No dataset, task or evaluation scenario is added or removed, including in the appendices.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: one- and eight-head standard attention for regression, standard attention/SWA/Global + SWA for language modeling, and standard attention for forecasting.

E3.justification: Experimental settings and metrics are unchanged. For example, Section 5.1 retains six layers, batch size 4, context length 1024 and head dimension 64; Appendix I retains ETTh1 horizons 96, 192 and 336 and the same tuning search.

E4.justification: The learning-rate sweeps, rank and width analyses, wall-clock comparison and forecasting-horizon analysis are retained unchanged in Figures 6-15. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the regression error bars for input dimension 16 in Appendix G and Figure 7. There are no new run-count disclosures, seeds or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The matched result plots, numerical values and reported findings are unchanged throughout Figures 2-15. Figure relocation does not add results or establish any performance change.

T1.justification: The matrix definitions, Definition 3.1, scoring equations and appendix derivations remain unchanged. 'Contiguous MLR' gives a more precise name to the already-defined unpermuted family without revising its mathematical construction or proofs.

C1.justification: The contributions concerning the rank bottleneck, distance-dependent compute and MLBTC unification remain substantively the same. The abstract, contribution list and discussion now explicitly name contiguous MLR, matching the family already defined by Equation (4).

C2.justification: The explanations of performance, task-dependent applicability, implementation-speed caveat and proposed future extensions are retained. No substantive new limitation, failure condition or interpretation of results is introduced.

D1.justification: Both PDFs provide the same code link and technical information, including contraction orders in Appendix D, initialization and normalization recipes in Appendix E, and forecasting tuning details in Appendix I.

R1.justification: Section 3.1 now explicitly relates the employed contiguous matrices to the unpermuted form of Parshakova et al.'s MLR family. The two associated references are updated to publication versions of the same works, rather than new cited studies.

P1.justification: The revision standardizes 'contiguous MLR', adds a short terminology explanation in Section 3.1, and makes limited wording, grammar and bibliography edits. The section sequence and overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1's subcaption/caption and Table 1's labeling adopt 'contiguous MLR'. Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, Figure 5 shifts within page 9, and later material repaginates. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves a terminology ambiguity by explicitly distinguishing the contiguous, unpermuted MLR family used in the paper from the broader terminology of the cited work. This improves precision and attribution. The methods, mathematical constructions and empirical support remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
